clignotement.name: Blink
clignotement.description: The bulb switches on and off endlessly. Useful as a timer visible from across the room.

gyrophare.name: Police lights
gyrophare.description: Alternating red and blue, like a police car. With two bulbs, they answer each other.

respiration.name: Breathe
respiration.description: Brightness rises and falls slowly, keeping the colour in place. Calm, for working.

bougie.name: Candle
bougie.description: A warm flame that flickers, never twice the same. The prettiest of the set.

orage.name: Storm
orage.description: A blue gloom, torn by white flashes at irregular intervals.

arc-en-ciel.name: Rainbow
arc-en-ciel.description: The hue turns gently around the whole colour wheel.

alerte.name: Alert
alerte.description: Three red flashes, then the lamp returns exactly as it was. To signal an event.

lever-de-soleil.name: Sunrise
lever-de-soleil.description: Five minutes from dark embers to broad daylight. Start it to wake up gently.

shared.title: One bulb, many keys
shared.body: Bulbs are declared once for the whole plugin. Every key picks from the same list: no need to retype the key each time, and a changed key is fixed in a single place.

stepHelp.title: What is the step for?
stepHelp.key: On a key, each press applies this step. A negative value makes a “dim” key: place two side by side, one at +10 and one at -10.
stepHelp.dial: On a dial, the step is the value of one detent; its sign is ignored, the direction of rotation decides.

tempHelp.title: Temperature landmarks
tempHelp.scale: 2700 K matches an incandescent bulb, very warm. 4000 K is a neutral white. 6500 K is daylight, cool and blue.
tempHelp.mode: Applying a temperature switches the bulb to white mode, so it leaves colour behind. The bulb imposes this, not the plugin.

colourHelp.title: How do key and dial behave?
colourHelp.key: On a key, one press turns the bulb on and applies exactly the colour chosen above. Place several for your favourite moods.
colourHelp.dial: On a dial, rotating turns the hue while keeping the bulb's current brightness. Pressing the dial toggles power.

scenarioHelp.title: How does it work?
scenarioHelp.toggle: One press starts the scenario, a second stops it. The lamp then returns exactly to the state it was in: same colour, same brightness, on or off.
scenarioHelp.second: Tick one bulb or several. Only Police lights has two roles today: with two bulbs they answer each other in red and blue, with one it alternates both colours on the same lamp, and any further bulb repeats the second role.
scenarioHelp.oneShot: Alert and Sunrise stop on their own, after three flashes and five minutes respectively. The others run until you press again.
scenarioHelp.safety: Animations are deliberately capped at two alternations per second: beyond that, flashing light can trigger a seizure in a photosensitive person.

cloud.title: Get my keys automatically
cloud.intro: Scan a QR code with the Calex or Smart Life app and every bulb on your account is added, keys included. Nothing to copy by hand.
cloud.where: In the app: Me → Settings → Account and security → User code
cloud.scan: Scan this in the app: + (top right) → Scan. Valid for about two minutes.
cloud.expired: The QR code expired before it was scanned. Try again.

scan.note: The search first listens for the announcements your bulbs broadcast, then, if nothing arrives, knocks at every address on the network. Allow about twenty seconds in the worst case. It finds address and identifier, but never the key: that one still has to be pasted once per bulb.
scan.none: No device found. Check that the bulb is powered and on the same network as this computer.
scan.sweep: (found by sweeping the network: your bulbs do not broadcast this far, which is common between a wired computer and a Wi-Fi bulb)

field.name: Name (optional) — e.g. Desk
field.keyKept: Leave empty to keep the key

save.ok: Bulb saved. Choose it in the list above.
save.needKey: This bulb needs its local key to be controllable.

twitch.intro: Viewers spend channel points to choose the colour of your bulbs. Connect your Twitch account once: LumenDeck creates the reward itself.
twitch.pairing: Check this code on the Twitch page that just opened:
twitch.waiting: Waiting for your approval on Twitch...
twitch.rewardOk: The reward is live on your channel. Change its cost or cooldown in your Twitch dashboard.
twitch.disconnectHelp: Disconnecting deletes the reward from your channel and removes LumenDeck's access.
twitch.bulbsHelp: These are the bulbs your viewers change. If none is ticked, the single declared bulb is used.
twitch.pauseHelp: Press the key to pause or resume viewers. While paused, every redemption is refunded.
twitch.inputHelp: Viewers type a colour name (red, blue, pink...) or a code such as #ff8800. Black and anything unreadable are refunded automatically.

outcome.unsettled: colour applied, but Twitch did not close it: settle it by hand in your dashboard
outcome.refundFailed: colour not applied, and Twitch refused the refund: refund it by hand in your dashboard

err.network: Twitch cannot be reached. Check your connection.
err.missing-scope: A permission was refused. Connect again and accept both.
err.reconnect-needed: Your Twitch session has expired. Connect again.
err.revoked: Access was removed on Twitch. Connect again.
err.forbidden: Twitch refused this account. Channel points need Affiliate or Partner status.
err.duplicate: A reward with this name already exists on your channel and was not created by LumenDeck. Rename or delete it, then try again.

reward.colorPrompt: Type a colour name (red, blue, pink...) or a code like #ff8800. Anything else is refunded.
